exposure: Type of insurance (public/Medicaid vs. commercial private insurance)
outcome: Self-reported experiences relating to autonomy, control, and respectful treatment in maternity care
Engagement in decision making regarding interventions (e.g., VBAC, episiotomy)
Likelihood of being consulted before episiotomy
Likelihood of feeling pressure to have a primary cesarean
Likelihood of being encouraged by staff to make own decisions
cohort: The study included 2,318 women in California with commercial private insurance (1,087) or public (Medi-Cal) (1,231) coverage, whose sampling frame was drawn from 2016 California birth certificate files.
finding: Women with public insurance (Medi-Cal) in California reported less control over their maternity care experience and less opportunity to choose their care compared to women with commercial insurance.
mod_finding: Women with Medi-Cal reported less choice for a vaginal birth after cesarean, were less likely to be consulted before an episiotomy, and were more likely to report feeling pressure to have a primary cesarean.
cross-section timing: The survey data represented experiences related to births in 2016 in California.
